fields.h1: Build a Feature Request Form Your Product Team Can Triage
fields.hero_description: Build a feature request form that files each request under a product area and tells the requester when it ships.
fields.features_heading: What Product Teams Need From Each Request
fields.features_subheading: "Add dark mode" alone leaves a product manager guessing. These six pieces collect the reason and report back to the requester.
fields.feature_1:
Questions set by the product area

The requester picks the part of the product the idea touches, such as Calendar or Billing. The form then asks what that team needs to know and files the request there.
fields.feature_2:
Similar requests shown before submit

As the requester types a title, the form lists open requests in the same area with their vote counts. One click adds a vote to an existing one, with the note saved under it.
fields.feature_3:
The problem asked before the solution

The first question asks what the person was trying to get done when the product fell short. Their suggested fix comes second. The team weighs the need apart from any one design.
fields.feature_4:
Contract value on logged requests

Account managers log requests for a customer and pick the account. The app looks up its contract value in HubSpot through the API and saves the figure on each request.
fields.feature_5:
A triage queue with one status each

Requests land in a queue sorted by area, votes or contract value. Each carries one status: Under review, Planned, Merged, Declined, or Shipped. A merge moves the votes along.
fields.feature_6:
An email when the feature ships

When a request moves to Shipped, the app emails everyone who asked or voted, with a link to the release note. A Declined status sends the reason the product manager wrote.

fields.tab_content_1:
Marisela's vote turns 46 into 47 on one request

Marisela Takeda runs the front desk at a physical therapy clinic on Quillbrook Scheduling. She picks Calendar on the feature request form and types "repeat bookings". The form shows Recurring appointments, an open request with 46 votes. She adds her vote with a note about weekly patients, and the count reads 47.
fields.tab_content_2:
Bulk edit, asked for by 3 accounts worth $210,000

Pellmark Logistics pays Tessellate Analytics $84,000 a year and wants to edit 200 shipments at once. Account manager Cassius Quintrell logs the request and picks Pellmark from the account list. The app pulls the contract value from HubSpot. Bulk edit now has 3 accounts behind it, worth $210,000 a year together.
fields.tab_content_3:
Before standup, 23 requests each get a status

Every Monday at Hollowpine Docs, product manager Esperanza Vossberg opens the week's new requests. This week there are 23. She moves 5 to Planned and merges 4 into older requests, which take their votes along. The other 14 stay Under review, and standup starts with every request labeled.
fields.tab_content_4:
All 31 dark mode requesters hear it shipped

Dark mode was asked for by 31 people at Lanternfield Notes, a note-taking app. When the product manager moves the request to Shipped, the app sends all 31 an email that points to the release note. Wilhelmina Haldane, who voted for it, turns dark mode on within the hour.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Feature Request Form
fields.howto_description: Follow 7 steps to build a feature request form that sorts each idea by product area and reports back to every requester.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write a reply for each status
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the parts of the product that one team owns, such as Search or Reports. Each becomes a choice on the form. Keep the list short enough that a customer finds the right area without asking support.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask what the person is trying to get done and what they do today instead. A workaround that takes an hour a week tells the team more than a vote does. Put the suggested design last, as an optional field.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Customers can reach the form from a link inside the product. Account managers and support staff log requests for the customers they look after. Their version of the form needs an account field.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the statuses a request can hold, and write the message each one sends. A decline should carry a real reason in a sentence or two. Shipped should link to the release note or help article.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the areas and statuses in one prompt, along with the questions each area asks. Emergent builds the feature request form and the triage screen behind it. To change a question later, ask in plain English.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect HubSpot or whichever CRM holds your contracts. The app reads each account's contract value through the CRM's API, and requests logged by account managers carry that figure into triage.
fields.howto_step_7_des: File a test request, then start the same idea again from another email address. The second attempt should offer a vote on the first. Move the original to Shipped and check that both test inboxes get the email.

faq_plan.q: What is a feature request form?
faq_plan.a: A feature request form is the standard way a product team collects requests for new functionality. Atlassian defines a feature request as a request a customer, stakeholder, or employee submits when they want to see a specific feature added to a product or service. The form asks for the same details every time, starting with the product area and the problem behind the idea.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a feature request form?
faq_plan.a: Start by listing your product areas and the statuses each request moves through. Describe both in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder, and say who is allowed to submit. Emergent builds the form and a triage queue for the product team, and every request is saved in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What fields belong in a feature request form template?
faq_plan.a: Start with five: the product area, a short title, the problem the person is trying to solve, how they work around it today, and an email for updates. That matches Atlassian's advice that well written requests clearly describe the problem, provide context, suggest solutions, and highlight benefits. The internal version also needs an account field.

faq_plan.q: What should a feature request form leave out?
faq_plan.a: Leave out anything the product team cannot act on. A customer who wants money back belongs on a refund request form, and a report that something is broken belongs with support. Skip a how-urgent-is-this scale as well, since the workaround question tells you more about the cost of waiting.

faq_plan.q: How do you prioritize requests from a feature request form?
faq_plan.a: Weigh the number of requesters against the revenue behind them and the effort to build. A request from 3 large accounts can outrank one with 40 votes from free users. Score effort with engineering before the request moves to Planned, not after. An app built with Emergent can pull each account's contract value from your CRM through its API.

faq_plan.q: How should a feature request form handle duplicate requests?
faq_plan.a: Merge each one into the original and keep every requester attached. The votes and notes from the copy move to the surviving request, and everyone who asked hears when its status changes. Showing similar open requests before someone submits gives them a chance to vote instead of filing a copy.

faq_plan.q: Can a feature request form work for internal tools?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Atlassian notes that employees can also submit feature requests inside their own company to suggest new features for their software and tools. An operations team asking for a new filter on an internal dashboard fits the same form, with the tool's name as the product area. A broken printer or a leaking pipe is a different job for a maintenance request form.

faq_plan.q: What should a feature request form send when a request is declined?
faq_plan.a: Send a short reply that says no plainly, gives the reason in a sentence, and points to any workaround. A line such as "Offline mode is off this year's roadmap while sync is rebuilt" is enough. If the answer could change later, keep the request open for votes and say so in the reply.

faq_plan.q: Should a feature request form be public or private?
faq_plan.a: Private is the safer default, and public helps when you want customers voting on each other's ideas. A public list also shows anyone outside the company what customers want next. A middle path is a private form with only Planned and Shipped items shown publicly. Forms built on Emergent have no response caps, however many ideas arrive.

faq_plan.q: Who should be able to fill out a feature request form?
faq_plan.a: Anyone who uses the product, plus the staff who speak for customers, such as support agents and account managers. Give staff their own version with an account field, which puts the customer's name on each request they log. A customer asking the company to do work for them, like setting up an integration, is not a feature request: send that to a service request form.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is one vendor's own wish form, two template roundups, a glossary definition, a sample form with three fields, a SaaS blog on collecting requests and a forum thread asking what to collect. None of them shows what happens after a request is submitted. This page wins for product teams by showing a working feature request form that sends each request to a product area, offers similar requests to vote on before a duplicate is filed, attaches the account's contract value to requests logged by account managers, feeds a weekly triage queue with statuses, and emails every requester when their feature ships, with every request in a database the team owns.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Feature Request Form Your Product Team Can Triage'; hero 'files each request under a product area and tells the requester when it ships' covers intake to ship, not one feature.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is templates, a definition and collection advice; page gives the definition (FAQ 1), the fields (FAQ 3 'Start with five: the product area, a short title...'), a 7-step how-to and the triage-to-ship flow none of them show.

specificity.evidence: Product-team vocabulary throughout: 'Under review, Planned, Merged, Declined, or Shipped', 'contract value', 'release note', 'standup'.

openers.evidence: Full-sentence openers: 'The requester picks the part of the product...', 'Every Monday at Hollowpine Docs...', 'List the parts of the product that one team owns'.

craft.evidence: Varied sentence lengths, no tacked-on endings; QC Q5-Q8 clean. 'A merge moves the votes along.'

voice.evidence: Calm, product-led: 'A workaround that takes an hour a week tells the team more than a vote does.' No hype verbs or summary lines.

truth.evidence: All 3 Atlassian statements match their quoted spans in domain_sources (FAQ 1, 3, 7); HubSpot lookup under api-connect; 'no response caps' under no-caps; numbers 46+1=47, 84,000+126,000=210,000, 5+4+14=23, 31 agree in copy and image checks.

distinct.evidence: Owns product-area intake, contract value and ship notices; app-feedback-survey (in-app screen surveys) and beta-landing-page (tester signups) do not overlap; suggestion-form overlap is a note below.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions answered first sentence, e.g. 'Merge each one into the original and keep every requester attached.' Hub link in item 2; no brand names in questions.
